_comment: Every ES2015-ES2023 built-in (Annex B included) the pinned Hermes lacks. The hermes-builtins ctest row probes the engine and fails unless its missing set is exactly this list, so a Hermes pin that gains or loses one fails the suite rather than drifting.

plugin-legacy picks core-js polyfills for the browsers in `targets`, not for Hermes, and every browser those targets name has these -- so none would be included. screenkit() adds each entry's `polyfill` (a core-js module) to the legacy polyfills bundle explicitly. An entry without one says why it cannot be polyfilled.

missing.why: The engine does not honour @@species, so defining the symbol would only make species checks lie -- and core-js reads a lying check as a broken native and swaps in slower Array methods.
Only a `with` statement reads it, and hermesc refuses `with` at build time.

No standalone core-js module sets it: only es.promise does, by replacing the engine's native Promise, which a toString tag does not justify. Object.prototype.toString.call(aPromise) reads [object Object].
Shared memory needs a second thread to share with, and there are no Workers (runtime/js/README.md). Not polyfillable.
Operates on SharedArrayBuffer, which does not exist here. Not polyfillable.
Bytecode carries no source, so a compiled function prints as `function f(a0) { [bytecode] }`. Not polyfillable; code that parses function source breaks.
core-js has no polyfill for it. It recompiles a RegExp in place, a legacy API nothing measured uses.
